subject: SLA - regional maintenance proration & monthly credit banding
messages:
From: Elena Novak <elena.novak@stratus.ai>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@stratus.ai
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 16:12:00 +0100
Subject: Request: regional maintenance carveout + monthly credit cap

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we're finalizing our SOW, a couple of items remain blockers for procurement and our security/compliance reviewers. Two asks:  

1) We run production traffic in a single EU region initially. We need a limited maintenance carveout for rolling infra updates — specifically, Stratus is requesting that planned maintenance windows (up to 6 hours/month, scheduled with 72h notice) be treated as prorated uptime rather than counted as unplanned downtime. In short: planned maintenance should not trigger credits if notified per the window and schedule.

2) Our finance team requires a clear monthly cap on service credits for combined uptime + latency SLOs. They asked for a fixed cap equal to 10% of one month’s invoice for the first year to limit financial exposure while we scale.

Can you confirm Redwood’s flexibility here? We prefer to keep public-cloud vendor SLAs standard, but this is a must for our board sign-off. I’ve attached the redlined SLA template from our procurement team and a proposed maintenance cadence.

Cheers,
Elena

--
Elena Novak
Head of Procurement, Stratus AI
elena.novak@stratus.ai
+44 20 7946 0958

Attachments: Stratus_SLA_Redline_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Elena Novak <elena.novak@stratus.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: regional maintenance carveout + monthly credit cap

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear note and for sharing the redline. I copied Ben (account lead) and Laura (contracts) so we can review holistically. Short answers up front: we can be flexible on planned maintenance proration with clear operational guardrails, and we can propose a bounded monthly-credit model — but we have some suggested changes to preserve service incentives and fairness for other customers.

High-level counterpoints:  
- Planned maintenance: Redwood’s standard is to exclude scheduled maintenance outside the stated maintenance SLA windows only when changes are performed during a pre-agreed maintenance window and announced 72 hours in advance. We can accept your 6-hour/month window for the EU region as an explicit carveout if we define: (a) a rolling 30-day schedule file, (b) maximum of 2 unplanned maintenance events/month that may not be eligible for proration, and (c) explicit emergency-rollback requirements.

- Monthly cap on credits: a fixed cap is acceptable, but rather than a straight 10% of invoice we propose a tiered cap tied to severity buckets (P1 downtime vs latency regressions). That keeps incentives aligned: severe service failures still get material credit while smaller transient latency blips are limited. We suggest a blended cap that equals the greater of (i) 8% of one month’s invoice and (ii) monthly aggregated cap calculated by severity bands up to 12% in the event of multiple P1 incidents.

Next steps I propose: Ben will draft a short counterproposal doc and Laura will prepare clean redlines for your procurement team. If that works I’ll loop Legal for final review and we can aim for an executed amendment alongside the SOW.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0199

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Template_v3.pdf (pdf)
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: internal - proposed counter and negotiation playbook for Stratus

Team — drafting my suggested approach below before I send it to Elena. Thoughts welcome.

Summary of what I plan to propose:  
1) Maintenance proration: Accept their 6-hr/month EU maintenance window as a formal scheduled-window carveout provided Stratus publishes a 30-day rolling schedule and we get 72h notice. Add a clause that allows us to disallow proration for more than 2 maintenance events/month if they exceed the scope outlined in the schedule.

2) Monthly credit cap: Offer a two-line cap:  
   - Baseline cap: 8% of single-month invoice for P2/P3 latency and minor availability blips (tokenization/partial degradation).  
   - Severe incidents cap: up to 12% for aggregated P1 outages that meet the P1 definition (total regional unavailability > 30 minutes).  
   - Provide an annual aggregate floor clause: total credits billed in a rolling 12 months will not exceed 20% of total billed value for that period (protects Redwood from catastrophic exposure).

3) Latency SLOs: Maintain existing percentile-based latency SLOs (p95/p99) but add an explicit clause that short, scheduled maintenance windows are excluded from SLO calculations when posted per the schedule.

4) Escrow/appeal process: If Stratus disputes a credit calculation we will:  (a) provide request-for-evidence timeline (48h), (b) open a joint incident review, and (c) permit one contractual appeal per quarter.

I want our counter to feel balanced — protects Stratus against unexpected exposure but keeps incentives intact. I’m leaning to provide this as a one-page amendment and keep the main SLA language intact. Laura, can you pull the legal-safe phrasing for the annual aggregate cap?

Thanks — Ben
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Elena Novak <elena.novak@stratus.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, procurement@stratus.ai
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: regional maintenance carveout + monthly credit cap

Elena — following internal review, attached is a concise counterproposal that captures our ask and a clean redline for your procurement team. Key points:  

1) We will accept a 6-hour/month scheduled maintenance carveout for your EU region if you publish a 30-day rolling maintenance schedule and provide 72 hours’ notice. This scheduled window will be excluded from uptime and latency SLO calculations. Two out-of-band scheduled events that exceed the documented scope in a month will be considered for non-proration.

2) Monthly crediting structure (counter):  
   - Baseline band: up to 8% of one month’s invoice for non-P1 incidents (p95/p99 latency regressions, minor availability degradation).
   - Severe incident band: up to 12% of one month’s invoice for aggregated P1 outages (regional unavailability > 30 minutes).
   - Annual protection: rolling 12-month aggregate credit cannot exceed 20% of total billed value for that period.

3) We exclude scheduled maintenance (when posted with 72h notice) from SLO calculations; emergency maintenance will be evaluated case-by-case.

4) Dispute and evidence process: 48h initial evidence timeline, joint incident review, and one appeal per quarter on calculations.

Please see the attached PDF (Redwood_counter_SLA_amendment.pdf) for exact language. If that looks reasonable we can have Laura and your procurement team lock the redlines and send to Legal for final sign-off — aiming to tie this amendment to the SOW signature.

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if you want to walk through the severity bands.

Best,
Grace
